name: Mocoví (moco1246, Guaicuruan)
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (2 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim on Grondona 1998 printed p. 41 (p. (2) Deciding source: a 1998 fieldwork-based reference grammar (PhD dissertation) with a dedicated stress section — the best available description per Glottolog's bibliography; no instrumental or prosody-specific study of Mocoví surfaced. (3) The one genuinely missing cross-check, Gualdieri 1998 (Unicamp, phonology-focused), was located via the Nimuendajú record and downloaded open-access from the Unicamp repository; its ch. II states 'o acento não é distintivo e ocorre regularmente na última sílaba da palavra' (pp. 27-28), independently confirming fixed final stress with only irregular/loan exceptions. Two independent field descriptions

sources.citation: Grondona, Veronica Maria. 1998. A Grammar of Mocovi. PhD diss., University of Pittsburgh. Read pp. 21, 41-42 (sec. 2.7 Suprasegmentals - Stress), 185-190 and 279 (ch. 6 loanword stress) from the full 324-p.
sources.quote: "Stress in Mocovi is essentially predictable, falling on the rightmost vowel of the word. Where stress is predictable, it is not marked in the data unless a word deviates from the predictable stress pattern. It is marked in examples (133)-(136) to illustrate the shift of stress to the rightmost vowel when suffixes and clitics are added to the end of a word." (p. 41). Also p. 41: "they follow Mocovi stress patterns: stress falls on the last vowel of the word." Exceptions are lexical loans only: S
sources.locator: printed p. 41 (p. 53), sec. 2.7 Suprasegmentals - Stress; exx. (133)-(138) pp. 41-42

sources.citation: Gualdieri, Cecilia Beatriz. 1998. Mocoví (Guaicurú): fonologia e morfossintaxe. Tese de doutorado, Universidade Estadual de Campinas (IEL), orient. Lucy Seki. 329 pp. DOI 10.47749/T/UNICAMP.1998.131859 (open, Unicamp repository; image-only scan, ch. II scanned to)
sources.quote: 'Visto que o acento não é distintivo e ocorre regularmente na última sílaba da palavra, será registrado apenas nas transcrições fonéticas e nos casos irregulares.' (Stress is non-distinctive and falls regularly on the last syllable of the word; marked only in phonetic transcriptions and irregular cases.) No dedicated stress section exists in the chapter (TOC pp. 7-8 checked; scanned sweep of printed pp. 27-85 finds no further stress rule, weight condition or secondary stress).
sources.locator: printed pp. 27-28 (pp. 28-29), cap. II Fonologia, sec. 1.1 Os fonemas; verified on page scan
sources.note: The only other modern phonological description of Mocoví and the cross-check the compilers note flagged as 'pin still needed'; downloaded now and it independently states regular final-syllable, non-distinctive stress (pp. 27-28) — add as second source on the record.

sources.citation: Juárez, Cristian R. (2019). Documentation and description of Northern Chaco Mocoví (Guaycuruan, Argentina). Endangered Languages Archive.
sources.note: This is a corpus deposit, not a grammar: the collection page lists 146+ open-access bundles (62 audio, 58 video, 26 images; titles such as 'A conversation about hunting in the field', 'Color concepts and locative markers', 'Directionals and locatives', 'Flexibles relations in Mocoví (Guaycuruan): Morphology and lexicon', 'Data collection materials') for Northern Chaco Mocoví. There is no collection description, abstract, grammar sketch, phonology write-up or PDF on the page, so it contains no statement about word stress. Glottolog's 'grammar' tag is a mislabel for a documentation corpus. Two…
